issues.detail: The Hebrew place name רִתְמָה (Rithmah) is rendered as 利瑪哈 (Lǐmǎhā), which is a transliteration error — the Hebrew has a ת (t) not a מ (m) in the second syllable, so it should be something like 利特瑪 (Rithmah). The Chinese 利瑪哈 changes the name's consonants.

The Hebrew place name רִמֹּן פָּרֶץ (Rimmon-perez) is rendered as 帕列茨石榴樹林 ('Perez pomegranate grove'), which reverses the order of the two elements: the Hebrew is 'Rimmon (pomegranate) of Perez' or 'Rimmon-perez', with Rimmon as the primary name and Perez as a qualifier. The Chinese puts Perez first and adds 石榴樹林 (pomegranate grove) as a descriptive gloss, which is not in the Hebrew and changes the proper name into a descriptive phrase.
